A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NuWa for deriving class-specific edge vision transformers, despite a substantial redesign in v2. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, inference-latency, ablation, and visualization results in Sections 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original accuracy, derivation-cost, deployment-efficiency, ablation, and robustness results, including detection and segmentation experiments.

M1.justification: V1 uses one-shot depth/classifier/head pruning followed by iterative pruning of four other dimensions and recovery fine-tuning. V2 introduces Self-Knowledge Purification through learned masks on frozen weights, followed by Optimization-based Fast Pruning. It retains QK/VO SVD compression but adds activation-based neuron selection and least-squares MLP reconstruction; post-pruning fine-tuning becomes optional.

E1.justification: ImageNet and both CIFAR datasets remain. V2 adds COCO2017 detection, instance segmentation, and multi-label classification, plus long-tailed ImageNet scenarios (Figure 7 and Supplement Section 13). V1's deliberately selected similar-class hard subtasks are no longer evaluated explicitly.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates Random, X-Pruner, and NViT. V2 retains Random and X-Pruner, removes NViT from the evaluated comparisons, and adds Magnitude Structured Pruning, Wanda-sp, Numerical Pruning, DC-ViT, RECAP, and MDP (Figure 6 and Table 1). NViT remains cited, which does not preserve its comparator participation.

E3.justification: V1's main evaluation uses ten hard/simple subtasks and pruning rates 0.20-0.80; v2 uses nine random 10/25/50-class subtasks, with training-dependent comparisons at 0.40 and 0.60. Five-epoch recovery is replaced by default evaluation without post-pruning retraining and optional ten-epoch fine-tuning. Latency testing changes from V40/Intel CPU at batch 256 to Orin NX at batch 1 and RTX 4090 at batch 256. Deployment-cost simulations are added.

E4.justification: V1's classifier-only comparison, structural-dimension ablations, neuron examples, depth analysis, and attention visualizations are largely removed. V2 adds SKP/component ablations, module-placement tests, calibration-sampling and target-architecture comparisons, batch-size and learning-rate sensitivities, derivation breakdowns, and long-tail/co-occurrence analyses. These investigate substantially different mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: V1 reports individual subtask results and averages without explicit uncertainty estimates. V2 Figure 4 explicitly reports means with standard-deviation bands across three random 25-class subtasks. This adds limited variability reporting without establishing repeated-seed experiments or significance testing.

E6.justification: The result sets are substantially replaced and expanded. V1 Table 4 reports 87.45% aggregate accuracy at 0.80 pruning and a 2.79x V40 speedup. V2 Table 2 reports 93.16% average accuracy versus X-Pruner's 93.77% under its new evaluation, alongside derivation costs; additional results cover memory, throughput, COCO, and robustness. Changed methods, subtasks, and settings prevent interpreting these as direct version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V1 contains Taylor importance approximations, SVD derivations, and bias-aware/joint-SVD formulations. V2 retains the SVD idea and relocates Taylor pruning to background material, but adds explicit low-rank and MLP least-squares optimization objectives and two supplementary optimality proofs (Section 10). The earlier bias-aware and joint-SVD derivations disappear.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on task relevance across seven structural dimensions and improved accuracy/inference speed through tailored pruning. V2 centers them on identifying class-detrimental weights, closed-form pruning without post-pruning retraining, and inexpensive large-scale derivation. Its headline comparison becomes near training-dependent accuracy with much lower derivation cost, alongside superiority to training-free baselines.

C2.justification: V1 interprets performance through dimension-specific task relevance and uneven knowledge distribution across layers. V2 emphasizes suppression of non-target outputs, detrimental knowledge in MLPs, and reuse of intermediate pruning computations. Supplement Section 15 adds explicit limitations for pruning beyond roughly 70% and larger subtasks, with proposed retraining and hypernetwork remedies.

D1.justification: V2 provides two pseudocode algorithms, tabulated SKP/OFP hyperparameters, calibration-sampling details, Swin-specific budget allocation, and dimensions rounded to multiples of eight. These replace much of v1's threshold-decay, recovery, and bias-aware SVD documentation. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named NuWa GitHub project.

R1.justification: The related-work framing changes from mask-based versus score-based pruning to training-free versus training-dependent methods, emphasizing detrimental-weight removal and derivation efficiency. V2 substantially expands discussion of compensation-based and language-model pruning, recent ViT baselines, and heterogeneous edge deployment. V1's knowledge-neuron and early-exit positioning largely disappears.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method, experiments, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around SKP/OFP and derivation cost. Background becomes Related Works, and Appendix A is replaced by a reorganized supplement containing proofs, implementation details, pseudocode, and limitations. The title changes from task-specific to class-specific, with author and affiliation updates.

P2.justification: The seven-dimension overview and most earlier analytical graphics are replaced by new SKP/OFP schematics, comparison diagrams, cost plots, and robustness displays. Accuracy tables are redesigned, deployment tables add throughput and memory columns, and algorithm boxes appear. The single-column appendix becomes a two-column supplement, constituting a substantial visual and layout revision.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable task/baseline coverage, direct Jetson measurements, derivation-cost evidence, and explicit limitations. However, removing v1's classifier-only comparison while suppressing non-target logits leaves attribution of SKP's gains less clear. New reproduction and theory material also contains inconsistencies: Algorithm 2 line 12 reverses the required neuron-removal budget, and Equation 32 uses a transpose where the preceding projector requires a pseudoinverse. These empirical gains and validation/reproducibility weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
